concept.name: Fade strategy
concept.definition: A contrarian tactic that trades against the prevailing move - selling into strength or buying into weakness - on the premise that the late stages of a move are driven by slow-reacting traders and prone to reversal. Common applications include fading overextended intraday moves and fading the initial reaction to economic data releases.
concept.intuition: If everyone who wanted to buy has already bought, the marginal flow runs out and the move stalls; fading is selling the exhaustion of a crowded move rather than its beginning.
concept.mechanics: Identify an extended move (a news spike, vertical run, or stretched deviation from a reference), enter against it with a defined invalidation beyond the extreme, and target reversion toward the pre-move level or a mean. Fading economic releases typically waits for the first reaction to complete before entering against it, with wider stops to survive post-release volatility.
concept.failure_modes: Trends persist far beyond apparent exhaustion, so fading strong trends produces repeated losses punctuated by occasional large ones when the trader averages into the fade; on regime-changing news the reversal simply never comes.
concept.misconceptions: That fading is synonymous with recklessness; disciplined fades use the same invalidation-first construction as any other setup, but it is a regime-dependent framework rather than a validated general edge.
concept.example: After a payrolls beat sends USD/JPY up 80 pips in minutes, a fade trader sells the pair once momentum stalls, targeting a retrace of half the spike with a stop above the reaction high.
